My own I6 spec amendment contradicted itself twice, and W1b's executor had to rule against the illustrative text to build against the normative text: acceptance.locked_sheet carried 65 hex characters (a sha256 is 64), and §4.2's chevron declared both `within` and `disjoint_from` against the same control, which §4.5 invariant 6 — added in the same commit — forbids. Both fixed (0d783b0). The old chevron literal now lives on as the known-broken fixture for HIT002, so the contradiction became a regression test.

I wrote a justification into aodex's SDK-03 gate claiming main_e2e.dart's probe block is compiled out unless EDEN_PROBE is set. No such guard exists and there is no probe code at all — strip the comments and the file is byte-identical to main.dart. The conclusion held; the argument was false. Caught by /code-review, not by the gate's own digest — which documents this as exactly what it cannot catch. Corrected in ef2c1a88.

I briefed the liveness check as 'an interactive control must publish at least one tap action'. Wrong: RenderIgnorePointer sets isBlockingUserActions, stripping the inner route while the outer Semantics(onTap:) survives — so each dead button published exactly one well-formed action. The rule would have been written from the incident and never fired on it. Corrected to assert reachability (e4bfff9). Caught because the implementer dumped the semantics tree instead of trusting my premise.
